title: Contextual mini-map and sparse navigation experiment
content:
Overview

Goal: test a lightweight, context-aware mini-map (visual map of the current area + quick jump actions) combined with a sparse primary navigation that surfaces only high-level roots and lets the mini-map provide detail. Objective is to reduce perceived complexity for new users while keeping power users able to deep-link and keyboard-navigate quickly.

Why this experiment now
- Current left rail is dense and long; new teams report overwhelm on first login.
- Analytics: high bounce on first session between 10–60s, many users jump to search instead of using nav.
- Hypothesis: exposing contextual structure near the page content (mini-map) + collapsing non-essential rails reduces cognitive load and improves task completion for new/occasional users while keeping discoverability.

Design concept (high level)
- Primary rail: sparse set of roots (Home, Workloads, Models, Routes, Observability, Billing, Settings). Icons + single-line labels.
- Contextual mini-map: small, persistent panel anchored under page header (or as a flyout on smaller widths). Shows a visual tree of the current root, highlights current page, quick actions (create, search within, filter), and breadcrumbs.
- Route contracts: pages declare a compact route contract (id, displayName, parentId?, canBeMiniMapped true/false, preferredActionSet: [create, annotate, rollback]) — runtime picks what to show.
- Deep link behavior: direct deep links open the mini-map expanded and highlight the node. Back/forward restores previous mini-map state.
- Mobile: mini-map becomes a slide-over modal; primary rail collapses to bottom tab bar (roots only).

Wireframe notes (sketch to dev QA)
1) Dashboard (Workloads root)\- Mini-map shows cluster > pool > instance > job nodes. Current page (job detail) highlighted. Quick actions: Re-run, View logs, Snapshot.\- Interaction: hover node shows small preview; click node navigates.
2) Model catalog\- Mini-map shows model families and pinned versions. Quick actions: Pin version, Start eval.\- Search box in mini-map uses same backend as top-level search but scoped to the root.
3) Routes page (routing policies)\- Mini-map shows active policies grouped by environment (prod/staging/experimental).\- Sticky filter row inside mini-map for environment and SLA tier.

Edge cases and behavior rules
- When user has <= 4 roots (e.g., small org): show full labels in primary rail by default.
- Permission-aware nodes: mini-map hides nodes user cannot access but shows greyed parent and a tooltip with request-access shortcut.
- Long names: truncate with accessible tooltip (aria-describedby) and full name in mini-map detail panel.
- Offline / slow connections: show skeleton mini-map and allow fallback to classic sidebar (feature-flag toggle).

Accessibility notes
- Mini-map must be keyboard operable: arrow keys to traverse nodes, Enter to open, Space to reveal quick actions.
- Announce expanded/collapsed node labels with live region.
- Contrast: ensure mini-map glyphs meet AA for small sizes.
- Screen-reader flow: allow linearized mini-map list (option in user preferences) for SR users.

Telemetry & success metrics
Primary metrics (A/B):
- New-user task completion rate (onboarding flow tasks).
- Time to first successful API call or model deploy from console (seconds).
- Navigation switch rate: % of sessions using mini-map vs classic nav.
- Search fallback rate (user uses global search after nav attempts).
- Help center escalation: clicks to docs / contact support from nav.
Secondary metrics:
- Average route depth traversed per session.
- Keyboard navigation usage (key events per session).

Rollout plan & flags
- Feature flags: miniMapEnabled (org), miniMapMode (floating | inline | off), sparseRail (on | off).
- Bootstrapping: enable for internal beta orgs -> 5% public sample -> 25% -> 100%.
- Canary rollback triggers: 7-day increase in help center escalations >15% over baseline OR >10% drop in task completion.

Backlog / TODOs (triage by priority)
- P0: Implement route contract interface + server-side metadata endpoint (fields: nodeId, label, icon, childrenCount, permissions). Acceptance: dev builds can render a sample mini-map from mocked endpoint. (Owner: Marcus)\- P0: Keyboard traversal primitives in UI kit. Acceptance: pass accessibility keyboard tests. (Owner: Lina)\- P1: Mini-map wireframes -> high-fidelity prototypes for Dashboard, Models, Routes. (Owner: Evelyn)\- P1: Permission-aware rendering logic & request-access shortcut.\- P2: Mobile slide-over adaptation and bottom-tab fallbacks.\- P2: Telemetry hooks (events: mini_map_open, node_click, quick_action_invoke, mini_map_search).\- P3: A/B test framework wiring and experiment dashboard queries.

Open questions / research items
- How to handle multi-root pages that logically belong to >1 root? (e.g., model-specific monitoring under Observability and Models) Proposed: allow node duplication with single source-of-truth id and cross-root pointers.
- Should mini-map support drag-to-pin nodes (persisted per-user)? Benefit: quick access to frequently used nodes. Cost: extra state; needs sync across devices.
- What is the acceptable width/height for inline mini-map on 1366x768? Need design research and prototyping.
- Localization: long labels in DE/FR may overflow; need test strings in prototype.

Implementation notes for engineering
- Keep mini-map virtualized for large trees; lazy-load child nodes on expand.
- Design tokens: reuse iconography and spacing from UI kit but add compact sizes API.
- Route contract should be a lightweight JSON blob; keep server-side generation at build time for static roots, dynamic for model/workload trees.

Next steps (this week)
- Design: produce 3 high-fidelity mockups (dashboard, model detail, routing policy) by Tue.\- Eng: spike on route contract and mocked endpoint by Thu.\- PM: finalize A/B metric definitions + experiment duration (suggest 4 weeks with min N=2000 new-user sessions).

Notes to reviewers
- This is exploratory: aim for a measurable reduction in onboarding friction rather than perfecting every nav edge case.
- Please add API/ux constraints inline as comments in the Figma file linked in linked_artifacts.

Quick links (work in progress)
- Prototype (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/mini-map-experiment\- Relevant tickets: CON-412 (route metadata), CON-425 (keyboard kit), CON-433 (telemetry events)

---
Status: rough draft -> needs design signoff and eng spike results before scheduling a canary rollout.

Unresolved: final tradeoff between inline mini-map vs flyout for medium widths (1024–1366).

End of doc.
